correctness.rationale: An edge changes ≤k coordinates and corrections can be done in k-blocks, so graph distance is rho=ceil(h/k), including all integer q≥2, d,k≥1. Fourier characters on (Z/q)^d yield Krawtchouk eigenvalues P_r(j) with multiplicity binom(d,j)(q−1)^j. If k=1 ordinary Hamming is a sum of squared Euclidean coordinate distances; if d≤k, complete graph is CND. Binary k=2 uses ceil(h/2)=h/2+(1−(−1)^h)/4, a sum of CND pieces. For binary d=k+1, distance J−I+antipodal matrix has nonconstant eigenvalues −1+(−1)^j≤0. Every other q≥3,k≥2 has isometric m=k+1 subcube with positive sector j=2 eigenvalue −1+(q−1)^(m−2)>0; remaining binary k≥3,d≥k+2 is excluded via m=k+2 subcube j=2 eigenvalue k−2>0. In first excluded dimensions D^p=J−I+(2^p−1)A, so maximizing positive nonconstant sectors gives α_q=log₂(1+(q−1)^−(m−2)), nullity binom(m,2)(q−1)²; binary M=m−1 odd or m−3 even, α=log₂(1+1/M), nullity 1 odd or binom(m,2)+m even. Embedding rank N−1−ν follows centered kernel, and Schoenberg/Gaussian finite Euclidean embedding gives strict PD exp(−tD^p) for t>0 inside interval (distinct points). p=0 convention explicitly checked. Independent integer exact character eigen tests of selected q,d,k corroborate, not prove general bounds.
